title: Tostones with Garlic Mojo
description: Green plantains fried once, smashed flat, and fried again so the edges shatter and the middle stays soft. The mojo alongside is raw — garlic, citrus, oil, nothing cooked.
notes: Green means green. A plantain with any yellow showing has started turning its starch to sugar, and it will brown long before it crisps.

steps.text: Crush the garlic to a paste with the sea salt, then stir in the olive oil, orange juice, lime juice, and dried oregano.
Leave the mojo to sit while you fry, so the raw garlic loses its edge.
steps.tip: Crushing with salt does the work a blender cannot — it breaks the cell walls without whipping air into the oil.

steps.text: Score the skin of the green plantains along their ridges, peel them under running water, and cut them into thick coins.
Fry the coins in the neutral oil over a moderate heat until pale gold and just tender, then lift them onto paper.
Smash each coin flat between two plates or a folded sheet of baking paper.
steps.tip: Smash them while they are hot. A cooled coin splits into three pieces instead of flattening.

steps.text: Dip each flattened piece briefly in the warm water, shake it off hard, and fry it again in hotter oil until it is crisp at the rim.
Drain them, hit them with the salt while they are still shining, and serve with the mojo.
